voices.name: Snare drum
voices.notes: Shares a channel with RIM; snare has priority if both are on one step.

voices.notes: Cannot sound on the same step as SNARE (snare wins).

voices.label: CLOSED HH
voices.name: Closed hi-hat

voices.label: OPEN HH

voices.label: CLAPS(TRIG)
voices.name: Handclaps
controls: TRIG OUT jack fires on every CLAPS step; a plug in TRIG OUT mutes the claps

accent: Number key 1 ACCENT (left of BASS) is written into steps like an instrument. Manual p.14: if you put an accent in a step then all instruments played on that step sound louder (one fixed accent level; global per step). Vintage Synth Explorer's claim of an accent control for each sound conflicts with the manual.
global_features: Built-in effects: none
9 PCM sounds; 8-bit at 15.6 kHz and 8-voice polyphony per Vintage Synth Explorer (not stated in the manual pages read)
Volume knobs: MASTER, HH CYMBAL (hi-hat + cymbal), METRONOME; tempo COARSE + FINE knobs
No per-voice level, tuning, pan, flam or shuffle documented
32 patterns of 1-2 bars: 01-16 up to 32 steps, 17-32 up to 16 steps
Resolution per pattern: 1/16 (4 steps/beat), 1/16 triplet (6 steps/beat), 1/32 (8 steps/beat)
6 songs (pattern chains with repeats)
Outputs: STEREO R/MIX and L, PHONES; internal stereo placement of voices not documented
DIN SYNC in/out (Korg 48 ppqn per Hollow Sun; runs Roland 24 ppqn gear at double speed), START/STOP footswitch jack, TRIG OUT, cassette tape interface; no MIDI (KMS-30 sync box)
Year: 1984 (E&MM reviewed the DDM series in Oct 1984); Hollow Sun and Vintage Synth Explorer say 1985
pack_contents: 18 one-shot WAVs, flat, no loops, all 44.1 kHz/16-bit. Two complete 9-voice sets. Set A (mono, named by voice): Ddm110Kick, Ddm110Snare, Ddm110Rimshot, Ddm110Tom_Hi, Ddm110Tom_Lo, Ddm110Hat_C, Ddm110Hat_O, Ddm110Cymbal, Ddm110Clap (0.07-0.70 s). Set B (stereo, generic names): Bassdrum, Snaredrum, Rim Shot, Tom-01, Tom-02, Hat Closed, Hat Open, Crash, Clap (0.08-0.78 s). Tom-01 is the higher tom and Tom-02 the lower (inferred from spectrum). No gaps.

preset_patterns.name: Manual step-time example 'Pattern number 01' (1/16 resolution, 8/4 = two bars of 4/4). Not a factory preset. Transcribed from the scanned step chart on manual p.15; CLAPS(TRIG) hit at step 21 (vs 20) is uncertain.
Factory demo patterns and demo song (loaded at the factory, also supplied on cassette); no charts published in the manual pages read

global_features: Built-in effects: none mentioned
Which voices share a channel or cut each other off: unknown (DDM-110 sister model has snare/rim and CH/OH priority pairs)
9 PCM Latin percussion sounds; soundprogramming.net lists 10 pads and 9 8-bit samples at 15.6 kHz (search snippet)
Volume controls: Master, Metronome, Cabasa/Tambourine; no per-voice level; no tuning; outputs L and R/MIX
32 patterns of 1-2 bars: 01-16 up to 32 steps, 17-32 up to 16 steps; resolution 1/16, 1/16 triplet or 1/32
Up to 6 songs, 390 bars in total (max 385 bars in one song)
DIN Sync socket with In/Out selector (syncs with DDM-110; KMS-30 for MIDI), Start/Stop footswitch socket, Trig Out (Tambourine steps), cassette interface
Year: reviewed Oct 1984 (E&MM); Hollow Sun says 1985

accent: Separate ACCENT row/track on Korg's programming sheet and an ACC row in nearly every factory chart. Polynominal says accent can be set for each instrument; a manual excerpt says to hold the ACCENT pad while playing an instrument to hear accent on that sound. Exact behaviour (global per step vs per instrument) is unresolved.
global_features: Built-in effects: none
8 analog sounds on 6 voice channels (Vintage Synth Explorer: 6-voice polyphony; Polynominal: up to 6 channels) - so some sounds share channels; open/closed hat sharing is unverified
Flam on HIGH TOM and LOW TOM
48 pattern memories = 3 groups (A, B, C) x 16 basic banks, up to 32 steps each; shipped with 48 preprogrammed rhythms (Korg Rhythm Charts)
Resolutions 1/16, 1/16 triplet, 1/32, 1/32 triplet (Polynominal)
Chains: 6 chain banks x 256 measures (Polynominal) vs two songs (Vintage Synth Explorer) - conflicting
Tempo 35-208 BPM (Polynominal); Korg suggests 6-8 on the tempo dial for the factory charts
DIN SYNC in/out at 48 ppqn (half speed vs Roland 24 ppqn), two +5 V trigger outs, cassette interface, battery or 9 V power
No shuffle or per-voice tuning documented
pack_contents: 'Korg KPR-77': 7 stereo one-shots (Bassdrum, Snaredrum, Tom H, Tom L, Hat Closed, Hat Open 1.54 s, Clap); no cymbal. 'Korg KPR77': 8 mono one-shots = full voice set (KPRKick, KPRSnare, KPRTom_Hi, KPRTom_Lo, KPRHat_C, KPRHat_O, KPRCymbal 1.37 s, KPRClap); five files carry smpl/inst root notes (Clap 36, Hat_C 37, Hat_O 38, Cymbal 42, Snare 43) that look arbitrary; three carry dBpoweramp tags dated 2003-11-15. All 44.1 kHz/16-bit, no loops.

built_in_effects.name: Effect 1
built_in_effects.notes: Digital multi-effect, 33 types (01-25 stereo, 26-33 dual): reverbs, early reflections, delays, chorus, flanger, phaser, tremolo, EQ, overdrive/distortion, exciter, ensemble, rotary speaker and combination types. Drum instruments panned to A, A:B or B feed the effects.

built_in_effects.name: Effect 2
built_in_effects.notes: Second multi-effect. Serial placement: A/B go through Effect 1 then Effect 2; C and D go unprocessed to outputs 3 and 4 but can be mixed into Effect 2 via PAN3/PAN4. Parallel placement: Effect 2 processes C and D. So drum instruments panned to C, C+D or D bypass Effect 1.

global_features: 4 Drum Kits edited in Global mode (F4-1 to F4-4); up to 30 instruments per kit (Index 0-29)

Per instrument: Inst (drum sound 01-44 or card sound), Key C0-G8, Tune -120..+120 in 10-cent steps (+/-1 octave), Level and Decay (table says -99..+99, text says -50..+50, relative to the Program's oscillator level and VDA EG decay), Pan/output A, A:B (9:1-1:9), B, C, C+D, D
Two sounds cannot share a key; one sound can sit on several keys; an assigned sound also fills unassigned keys below it (re-pitched)
A kit is played through a Program in Drum Kit mode; Program parameters (level, VDA EG, filter, effects) act on the whole kit
No exclusive/choke-group parameter on the drum kit page (inferred: hats do not cut each other)
Outputs 1/L, 2/R, 3, 4; PCM ROM 4 MB, 16-bit; 16 voices
Year 1988: widely documented but not checked against a fetched source here

One triangle LFO (MG) via the joystick; 256-step polyphonic step sequencer
E&SM (July 1985): drum synthesis is hard because lowering resonance to smooth DCO bass also loses the noise burst; percussive patch Voice 81 takes the filter out so DEG3 shapes a noise burst
